samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification and a numeral compound)
samasa.vigraha: पञ्च प्रेताः पञ्चप्रेताः; पञ्चप्रेताः एव आसनम् पञ्चप्रेतासनम्; पञ्चप्रेतासने आसीना पञ्चप्रेतासनासीना
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca pretāḥ pañcapretāḥ; pañcapretāḥ eva āsanam pañcapretāsanam; pañcapretāsane āsīnā pañcapretāsanāsīnā
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-preta 'the five pretas' (numeral compound). (2) pañcapreta-āsana 'the seat that is the five pretas', a karmadhāraya of identification: the five are themselves the seat. (3) The participle āsīnā 'seated' is the head and takes the seat in the locative: 'seated on the seat of the five pretas'.

components.note: appears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)

names.meaning: She who sits on the seat formed by the five corpses
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the five pretas are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara as the four legs of Her couch and Sadāśiva as its plank: without Her power even these gods are lifeless, and only as Her seat do they act.
names.previous_split_issues: pretāsanāsīnā was left as one row; it is preta + āsana + āsīnā, joined twice by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner numeral compound), followed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: पञ्च ब्रह्माणः पञ्चब्रह्माणः; पञ्चब्रह्मणाम् स्वरूपम् पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca brahmāṇaḥ pañcabrahmāṇaḥ; pañcabrahmaṇām svarūpam pañcabrahmasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti pañcabrahmasvarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-brahma 'the five Brahmās' (numeral compound; brahman drops its final n, 8.2.7). (2) …brahma-svarūpa 'the own form of the five Brahmās' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has the own form of the five Brahmās', i.e. who is their very nature. Juxtaposition throughout.

components.note: appears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)

components.meaning: here: one of the five Brahmās, the deities of the five cosmic acts
whose own form is, having the nature of
components.note: sva 'own' + rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine

names.meaning: She whose own form is the five Brahmās
names.significance: The same five gods who are Her lifeless seat in name 249 are, as active powers, nothing but Her own form: they act only as She acts through them.

meaning_check.note: 'Composed of' replaced by the sense of svarūpa 'own form'; 'brahmas' capitalized (Brahmās).

names.previous_split_issues: svarupiṇī (short u) was a misprint, now corrected in the text to svarūpiṇī; 'Brahma/Absolute' did not say which Brahmā is meant (the five deities of the cosmic acts).

sandhi.rule: a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

names.meaning: She who is consciousness itself
names.significance: She does not have consciousness as a quality; She consists of it, as Vedānta says of Brahman.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is cit + the suffix -mayī, with t → n before m.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: परमः आनन्दः परमानन्दः; परमानन्दः स्वरूपम् यस्याः सा परमानन्दा
samasa.vigraha_iast: paramaḥ ānandaḥ paramānandaḥ; paramānandaḥ svarūpam yasyāḥ sā paramānandā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: parama 'supreme' qualifies ānanda 'bliss' (karmadhāraya). Applied to Her it takes the feminine -ā, as a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose very nature is supreme bliss'.

names.meaning: She who is supreme bliss
names.significance: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad (3.6) teaches that Brahman is bliss, from which all beings arise; She is that bliss.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is parama + ānandā, fused by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), followed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: विज्ञानेन घनः विज्ञानघनः; विज्ञानघनम् रूपम् विज्ञानघनरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति विज्ञानघनरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: vijñānena ghanaḥ vijñānaghanaḥ; vijñānaghanam rūpam vijñānaghanarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti vijñānaghanarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) vijñāna-ghana 'dense with consciousness alone', a solid mass of consciousness (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) It qualifies rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has a form that is a mass of consciousness'.

names.meaning: She whose form is a solid mass of pure consciousness
names.significance: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.4.12) calls the Self 'vijñānaghana eva', nothing but a mass of consciousness, like a lump of salt that is salty through and through.

meaning_check.note: ghana is 'a solid mass, dense', not 'all-pervading'; vijñāna here is consciousness rather than 'intelligence'.

samasa.vigraha: ध्यानम् च ध्याता च ध्येयम् च ध्यानध्यातृध्येयानि; ध्यानध्यातृध्येयानि रूपम् यस्याः सा ध्यानध्यातृध्येयरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: dhyānam ca dhyātā ca dhyeyam ca dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyāni; dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyāni rūpam yasyāḥ sā dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyarūpā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: a dvandva of three derivatives of √dhyai 'to meditate' — dhyāna 'meditation', dhyātṛ 'meditator', dhyeya 'what is to be meditated upon'. Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose form is these three'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition throughout.

names.meaning: She whose form is meditation, the meditator and the object of meditation
names.significance: The triad of knower, knowing and known (tripuṭī) is all Her; when it is seen as one, meditation reaches its end.

meaning_check.note: 'Shines as' is not in the name; the bahuvrīhi says the three are Her form.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: धर्मः च अधर्मः च धर्माधर्मौ; धर्माधर्माभ्याम् विवर्जिता धर्माधर्मविवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: dharmaḥ ca adharmaḥ ca dharmādharmau; dharmādharmābhyām vivarjitā dharmādharmavivarjitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: dharma 'merit, virtue' and adharma 'demerit' form a dvandva. Outer layer: the participle vivarjitā 'wholly free from' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is devoid of (who transcends) both virtue and vice
names.significance: Merit and demerit bind only one who acts as a separate agent; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad speaks of That which is other than dharma and other than adharma.
names.previous_split_issues: dharmādharma was left fused; it is dharma + adharma.

samasa.vigraha: विश्वम् रूपम् यस्याः सा विश्वरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśvam rūpam yasyāḥ sā viśvarūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form is the universe'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition. In this sequence the name can also be read 'She who has the form of Viśva', the self of the waking state.

components.meaning: the universe, all; also Viśva, the waking self of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad

names.meaning: She who has the whole universe as Her form
names.significance: Names 256–263 follow the states of the self in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad; here She is the universe, and also Viśva, the self as experiencer of the waking world.
names.previous_split_issues: 'rupā' (short u) was a misprint, now corrected in the text to rūpā.

names.meaning: She who is in the waking state, or She who assumes the form of the jīva who is in the waking state
names.significance: Traditionally She is both the waking state itself and the individual (jīva) who experiences it.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'jIva' put into IAST.

names.meaning: She who is in the dream state, or She who assumes the form of the jīva in the dream state
names.significance: As dreamer She creates and enjoys a world of Her own making, a picture of how the whole universe is Her projection.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'jIva' put into IAST.

names.uncertain: By Pāṇini (7.1.80–81) the feminine participle of the class-2 root svap (svapiti) would be svapatī; svapantī follows the thematic inflection (svapati) found in epic usage. The text reads svapantī and the metre is the same either way.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: तैजसः आत्मा यस्याः सा तैजसात्मिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: taijasaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā taijasātmikā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose self is Taijasa'; ātman takes the suffix -ka and the feminine -ikā (a → i, Pāṇini 7.3.44).

components.meaning: Taijasa, 'the luminous one': the self in the dream state

names.meaning: She whose self is Taijasa, the dreaming self
names.significance: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad names the dreaming self Taijasa, 'the luminous', because in dream it is lit by its own light; it is identified with the subtle body.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'taijasA', 'jIva' put into IAST; 'soul of' turned the relation round (ātmikā = 'whose self is').

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is taijasa + ātmikā.

names.meaning: She who is in the deep-sleep state or assumes the form of the jīva experiencing deep sleep
names.significance: In deep sleep all distinctions rest in Her, as the world rests in Her at dissolution.

meaning_check.note: 'jiva' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: प्राज्ञः आत्मा यस्याः सा प्राज्ञात्मिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: prājñaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā prājñātmikā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose self is Prājña'; ātman takes -ka and the feminine -ikā, as in name 259.

components.meaning: Prājña, 'the knower': the self in deep sleep

names.meaning: She whose self is Prājña, the self in deep sleep
names.significance: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad calls the self in deep sleep Prājña, a mass of knowing made of bliss; it is identified with the causal body.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'prAj~nA' put into IAST; Prājña is the deep-sleep self, not deep sleep itself.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is prājña + ātmikā.

names.meaning: She who is the Fourth (turya), the state beyond waking, dream and deep sleep
names.significance: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad calls the Self beyond the three states 'the fourth': not a further state but the witness present in all three.

meaning_check.note: Wording tidied; turya is 'the fourth', the witness-consciousness, rather than a state in which realization 'is obtained'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाः अवस्थाः सर्वावस्थाः; सर्वावस्थाभिः विवर्जिता सर्वावस्थाविवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: sarvāḥ avasthāḥ sarvāvasthāḥ; sarvāvasthābhiḥ vivarjitā sarvāvasthāvivarjitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: sarva-avasthā 'all states' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: vivarjitā 'wholly free from' is the head and takes the states in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who transcends all states
names.significance: Traditionally this is the state beyond even the fourth (turyātīta): She is not touched by any state, the fourth included.
names.previous_split_issues: sarvāvasthā was left fused; it is sarva + avasthā.

samasa.vigraha: सृष्टेः कर्त्री सृष्टिकर्त्री
samasa.vigraha_iast: sṛṣṭeḥ kartrī sṛṣṭikartrī
samasa.explanation: kartrī 'maker', the feminine of the agent noun kartṛ, is the head and sṛṣṭi 'creation' stands to it in the genitive: 'the maker of creation'. Juxtaposition.

names.meaning: She who is the creator
names.significance: Names 264–274 set out the five cosmic acts — creation, protection, dissolution, concealment and grace — each with its presiding deity; here She creates, as Brahmā (name 265).
names.uncertain: Pāṇini 2.2.15 restricts compounding a genitive with an agent noun in -tṛ; compounds like sṛṣṭi-kartṛ are nevertheless standard in usage and are usually explained as a general genitive (śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī).

samasa.vigraha: ब्रह्मा रूपम् यस्याः सा ब्रह्मरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: brahmā rūpam yasyāḥ sā brahmarūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form is Brahmā'; brahman drops its final n in composition and rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: Brahmā, the creator (masculine); also Brahman, the Absolute (neuter)

names.meaning: She who has the form of Brahmā, the creator
names.significance: In the sequence of cosmic acts She creates as Brahmā; read with the neuter brahman, the name also says She is the Absolute itself.

meaning_check.note: In this sequence 'brahma' is Brahmā the creator (the deity of creation, name 264); the reading as Brahman is kept under significance.

names.previous_split_issues: brahma was glossed 'Brahma/Absolute' without saying which is meant here.

names.meaning: She who protects
names.significance: The second of the cosmic acts, protection or maintenance (sthiti), which She performs as Govinda (name 267).

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, followed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: गोविन्दस्य रूपम् गोविन्दरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति गोविन्दरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: govindasya rūpam govindarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti govindarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: govinda-rūpa 'the form of Govinda' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), with the possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has the form of Govinda'. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: Govinda, a name of Viṣṇu (traditionally 'finder of cows' or 'he who is known through speech')

names.meaning: She who has assumed the form of Govinda (Viṣṇu) for the preservation of the universe
names.significance: As Viṣṇu She sustains the worlds; the gods of the five acts are Her forms, not powers beside Her.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'viShNu' put into IAST.

sandhi.rule: the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

names.meaning: She who is the destroyer of the universe
names.significance: Saṃhāra is a 'drawing together': at dissolution She withdraws the worlds into Herself as a tortoise draws in its limbs.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is sam + hāriṇī.

samasa.vigraha: रुद्रः रूपम् यस्याः सा रुद्ररूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: rudraḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā rudrarūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form is Rudra'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: Rudra, Śiva as the lord of dissolution

names.meaning: She who has assumed the form of Rudra (Śiva) for the dissolution of the universe
names.significance: Dissolution, the third cosmic act, She performs as Rudra.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shiva' put into IAST; the stray 'is' removed ('who is has').

sandhi.rule: the s of tiras becomes u before a voiced consonant and combines with the preceding a as o (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca; 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: तिरोधानम् करोति इति तिरोधानकरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: tirodhānam karoti iti tirodhānakarī
samasa.explanation: -karī 'making, causing' (√kṛ with the suffix -a, feminine -ī) is the head and takes tirodhāna 'concealment' as its object. Tirodhāna itself is tiras 'out of sight' + dhāna 'placing', i.e. hiding from view.

names.meaning: She who brings about concealment (tirodhāna)
names.significance: Concealment, the fourth cosmic act, is the veiling by which She hides Her own nature so that the play of the world can go on; it is performed as Īśvara (name 271).

meaning_check.note: Tirodhāna is concealment, the veiling of the Self, not merely the 'disappearance of all things'.

names.previous_split_issues: tirodhāna was given as one row; it is tiras 'out of sight' + dhāna 'placing'.

names.meaning: She who is the Sovereign, Īśvarī
names.significance: In the sequence of the five acts She is the power of Īśvara, the deity of concealment; read on its own, the name makes Her ruler of all.

meaning_check.note: 'Protects' is not in the name; īśvarī is 'sovereign', and in this sequence the consort-power of Īśvara, deity of the fourth act (concealment).

samasa.vigraha: सदा शिवा सदाशिवा
samasa.vigraha_iast: sadā śivā sadāśivā
samasa.explanation: The indeclinable sadā 'always' qualifies śivā 'auspicious, benign', the head: 'ever auspicious'. As a name it is the feminine of Sadāśiva, the deity of the fifth act. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: auspicious, benign; the consort of Śiva

names.meaning: She who is Sadāśiva, the ever-auspicious
names.significance: Sadāśiva is the deity of grace (anugraha), the fifth act, named in the next name.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'sadAshiva' put into IAST; 'bestows' is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: sadā was glossed 'true/good'; it is the indeclinable 'always'.

samasa.vigraha: अनुग्रहम् ददाति इति अनुग्रहदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: anugraham dadāti iti anugrahadā
samasa.explanation: -dā 'giving' (√dā with the suffix -a, feminine -ā) is the head and takes anugraha 'grace' as its object.

components.meaning: grace, favor, blessing (lit. 'taking hold of after')

names.meaning: She who confers blessing
names.significance: Grace (anugraha) is the fifth cosmic act, which ends concealment and reveals the Self; it is the act by which She frees.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the n of ayana then becomes ṇ after the r of para (retroflexion)

samasa.vigraha: पञ्च कृत्यानि पञ्चकृत्यानि; पञ्चकृत्येषु परायणा पञ्चकृत्यपरायणा
samasa.vigraha_iast: pañca kṛtyāni pañcakṛtyāni; pañcakṛtyeṣu parāyaṇā pañcakṛtyaparāyaṇā
samasa.explanation: (1) pañca-kṛtya 'the five acts' (numeral compound). (2) parāyaṇā 'wholly given to, intent on' — itself para 'highest' + ayana 'goal', 'having as highest goal' — is the head and takes the acts in the locative.

components.note: appears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)
√kṛ + the gerundive suffix -ya: 'what is to be done'

names.meaning: She who is devoted to the five functions (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace)
names.significance: Names 264–273 have named the five acts with their deities; this name gathers them, for She alone performs them all.

meaning_check.note: The list of the five functions was wrong ('annihilation and reappearance'); they are creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace.

names.previous_split_issues: parāyaṇā was given as one row; it is para + ayanā.

samasa.vigraha: भानोः मण्डलम् भानुमण्डलम्; भानुमण्डलस्य मध्यम् भानुमण्डलमध्यम्; भानुमण्डलमध्ये तिष्ठति इति भानुमण्डलमध्यस्था
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhānoḥ maṇḍalam bhānumaṇḍalam; bhānumaṇḍalasya madhyam bhānumaṇḍalamadhyam; bhānumaṇḍalamadhye tiṣṭhati iti bhānumaṇḍalamadhyasthā
samasa.explanation: (1) bhānu-maṇḍala 'the disc of the sun' and (2) …maṇḍala-madhya 'its center' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (3) -sthā 'standing, abiding' (√sthā + -a, Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ) is the head and takes the center as its place.

components.note: √sthā 'to stand' + -a, feminine; only at the end of a compound

names.meaning: She who abides at the center of the sun's disc
names.significance: Traditionally She is meditated upon in the sun's orb at the twilight worship (sandhyā), as the light within the light; compare name 240, the moon's disc.
names.previous_split_issues: madhyasthā was left fused; it is madhya 'center' + -sthā 'abiding'.

components.meaning: the consort and power of Bhairava; the awe-inspiring one

names.meaning: She who is the wife of Bhairava (Śiva)
names.significance: Bhairavī is also the Goddess in Her own awe-inspiring form, worshipped as Tripurabhairavī among the great Wisdom Goddesses.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'shiva' put into IAST.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, followed by the possessive suffix -in
samasa.vigraha: भगानाम् माला भगमाला; सा अस्याः अस्ति इति भगमालिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhagānām mālā bhagamālā; sā asyāḥ asti iti bhagamālinī
samasa.explanation: bhaga-mālā 'a garland of excellences' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), with the possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has (wears) a garland of excellences'. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: excellence, fortune, glory; the six divine excellences

names.meaning: She who wears a garland made of the six excellences (of auspiciousness, supremacy, fame, valor, detachment and knowledge)
names.significance: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa defines bhaga as the six excellences — sovereignty, valor, fame, prosperity, knowledge and dispassion. Bhagamālinī is also the second of the fifteen Nityā goddesses of the Śrīcakra.
names.previous_split_issues: mālinī was glossed 'garlanded/possessing' without the noun mālā 'garland'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पद्मम् आसनम् यस्याः सा पद्मासना
samasa.vigraha_iast: padmam āsanam yasyāḥ sā padmāsanā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose seat is a lotus'; āsana takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She who is seated in the lotus flower
names.significance: Traditionally the lotus is also inward: She is seated in the lotuses (cakras) of the body, and in the thousand-petalled lotus above them.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is padma + āsanā.

components.note: the possessive suffix -mat, appearing as -vat after a stem in -a (Pāṇini 8.2.9), feminine -vatī

names.meaning: She who is the Blessed One, possessed of all six excellences
names.significance: The Viṣṇu Purāṇa calls Bhagavān the one who has the six excellences, and the one who knows the arising and dissolution of beings, their coming and going, knowledge and ignorance; She is Bhagavatī in that full sense.

meaning_check.note: 'Protects those who worship Her' is not in the name; bhagavatī means 'possessing bhaga', the six excellences (name 277).

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is bhaga + the suffix -vatī.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पद्मम् नाभौ यस्य सः पद्मनाभः; पद्मनाभस्य सहोदरी पद्मनाभसहोदरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: padmam nābhau yasya saḥ padmanābhaḥ; padmanābhasya sahodarī padmanābhasahodarī
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: padma-nābha 'He in whose navel is a lotus', Viṣṇu (bahuvrīhi; nābhi 'navel' takes the form nābha at the end of the compound). Outer layer: sahodarī 'sister' (lit. 'of the same womb') is the head and takes Him in the genitive.

components.note: appears as nābha- at the end of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is the sister of Padmanābha (Viṣṇu)
names.significance: Traditionally Pārvatī is Viṣṇu's sister; in Śrīvidyā the two are one power, appearing as Viṣṇu in male form and as the Goddess in female form.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'viShNu' put into IAST; the name Padmanābha restored.

names.previous_split_issues: nābha was glossed 'navel (Viṣṇu)'; padmanābha 'lotus-naveled' is Viṣṇu, and nābhi is the word for navel.

sandhi.rule: a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)
guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner itaretara-dvandva, a karmadhāraya of two participles and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: उन्मेषः च निमिषः च उन्मेषनिमिषौ; उत्पन्ना च विपन्ना च उत्पन्नविपन्ना; भुवनानाम् आवली भुवनावली; उन्मेषनिमिषाभ्याम् उत्पन्नविपन्ना भुवनावली यस्याः सा उन्मेषनिमिषोत्पन्नविपन्नभुवनावली
samasa.vigraha_iast: unmeṣaḥ ca nimiṣaḥ ca unmeṣanimiṣau; utpannā ca vipannā ca utpannavipannā; bhuvanānām āvalī bhuvanāvalī; unmeṣanimiṣābhyām utpannavipannā bhuvanāvalī yasyāḥ sā unmeṣanimiṣotpannavipannabhuvanāvalī
samasa.explanation: (1) unmeṣa-nimiṣa 'the opening and the closing (of the eyes)' (dvandva). (2) utpanna-vipanna 'arisen and perished', two participles joined as a karmadhāraya, taken in order with the dvandva: arising with the opening, perishing with the closing. (3) bhuvana-āvalī 'the row of worlds' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by whose opening and closing of the eyes rows of worlds arise and perish'.

names.meaning: She at the opening and closing of whose eyes whole rows of worlds arise and perish
names.significance: Creation and dissolution cost Her no more than a blink. In Kashmir Śaivism unmeṣa and nimeṣa are also the unfolding and infolding of consciousness, by which the world appears and withdraws.

meaning_check.note: Rendered as the bahuvrīhi it is: the worlds arise and perish with Her blink; 'causes' was an interpretation.

names.previous_split_issues: unmeṣa and nimiṣotpanna were not divided: un-meṣa (ut + meṣa) and nimiṣa + utpanna (guṇa); bhuvanāvalī is bhuvana + āvalī.
names.uncertain: A bahuvrīhi ending in an ī-stem like āvalī would by Pāṇini 5.4.153 normally take the suffix -ka (…āvalīkā); the name keeps -āvalī, which is common in such poetic compounds.

samasa.vigraha: शीर्षाणि च वदनानि च शीर्षवदनानि; सहस्रम् शीर्षवदनानि यस्याः सा सहस्रशीर्षवदना
samasa.vigraha_iast: śīrṣāṇi ca vadanāni ca śīrṣavadanāni; sahasram śīrṣavadanāni yasyāḥ sā sahasraśīrṣavadanā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: śīrṣa-vadana 'heads and faces' (dvandva). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi with the numeral sahasra 'a thousand': 'She who has a thousand heads and faces'; vadana takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

names.meaning: She who has a thousand heads and faces
names.significance: Names 282–284 echo the Puruṣa-sūkta of the Ṛgveda — 'sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt' — and give the cosmic Person's form to Her; 'thousand' means countless.
names.previous_split_issues: vadanā was glossed 'faced'; the member is vadana 'face', with the feminine ending of the bahuvrīhi.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: सहस्रम् अक्षीणि यस्याः सा सहस्राक्षी
samasa.vigraha_iast: sahasram akṣīṇi yasyāḥ sā sahasrākṣī
samasa.explanation: 'She who has a thousand eyes'. In a bahuvrīhi akṣi 'eye' takes the suffix -a (ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113), giving -akṣa, and the feminine is -ākṣī (4.1.41).

components.note: akṣi, as -akṣa in the bahuvrīhi, feminine -akṣī

names.meaning: She who has a thousand eyes
names.significance: Her eyes are everywhere: nothing happens unseen by Her.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is sahasra + akṣī, fused by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.vigraha: सहस्रम् पादाः यस्याः सा सहस्रपात्
samasa.vigraha_iast: sahasram pādāḥ yasyāḥ sā sahasrapāt
samasa.explanation: 'She who has a thousand feet'. After a numeral, pāda loses its final a in a bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 5.4.140) and becomes pād, whose nominative is pāt; the bahuvrīhi may keep this form in the feminine (4.1.8 pādo 'nyatarasyām).

components.note: pāda 'foot' as pād in the bahuvrīhi; nominative pāt

names.meaning: She who has a thousand feet
names.significance: With the Puruṣa-sūkta's thousand feet She stands in every place at once.
names.previous_split_issues: pāt was glossed 'footed'; it is pād 'foot', and the 'having' comes from the bahuvrīhi.

samasa.vigraha: ब्रह्मणः आरभ्य कीटपर्यन्तम् आब्रह्मकीटम्; आब्रह्मकीटम् सर्वेषाम् जननी आब्रह्मकीटजननी
samasa.vigraha_iast: brahmaṇaḥ ārabhya kīṭaparyantam ābrahmakīṭam; ābrahmakīṭam sarveṣām jananī ābrahmakīṭajananī
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: ā-brahma-kīṭa 'from Brahmā down to the worm', an avyayībhāva with the indeclinable ā 'up to, including' (Pāṇini 2.1.13 āṅ maryādābhividhyoḥ), naming every being between the two limits. Outer layer: jananī 'mother' is the head, with all those beings in the genitive. brahman drops its final n in composition.

names.meaning: She who is the mother of everything from Brahmā to the lowliest insect
names.significance: No being is too high or too low to be Her child: the creator himself and the smallest insect have the same Mother.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'brahmA' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: ābrahma was given as one row ('from Brahmā'); it is the indeclinable ā + brahma, and the limit ā governs brahma-kīṭa together.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: वर्णाः च आश्रमाः च वर्णाश्रमाः; वर्णाश्रमाणाम् विधायिनी वर्णाश्रमविधायिनी
samasa.vigraha_iast: varṇāḥ ca āśramāḥ ca varṇāśramāḥ; varṇāśramāṇām vidhāyinī varṇāśramavidhāyinī
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: varṇa-āśrama 'the classes and the stages of life' (dvandva). Outer layer: vidhāyinī 'she who ordains' (vi + √dhā with the agent suffix -in, y inserted after the ā, feminine -inī) is the head and takes them in the genitive.

components.meaning: stage of life (student, householder, forest-dweller, renunciant)

names.meaning: She who ordains the order of the classes and the stages of life
names.significance: Traditionally the order of duties belongs to Her because the Vedas that teach it are Her command (name 287).

meaning_check.note: 'Social division in life' was vague and ungrammatical; varṇa (class) and āśrama (stage of life) are rendered separately.

names.previous_split_issues: varṇāśrama was left fused (varṇa + āśrama); vidhāyini (short final i) was a misprint, now corrected in the text to vidhāyinī.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya)
samasa.vigraha: निजा आज्ञा निजाज्ञा; निजाज्ञा रूपम् येषाम् ते निजाज्ञारूपाः; निजाज्ञारूपाः निगमाः यस्याः सा निजाज्ञारूपनिगमा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nijā ājñā nijājñā; nijājñā rūpam yeṣām te nijājñārūpāḥ; nijājñārūpāḥ nigamāḥ yasyāḥ sā nijājñārūpanigamā
samasa.explanation: (1) nija-ājñā 'Her own command' (karmadhāraya). (2) nijājñā-rūpa 'having Her own command as their form', a bahuvrīhi qualifying nigama. (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose Vedas have the form of Her own command'; nigama takes the feminine -ā.

names.meaning: She whose own commands are the Vedas
names.significance: Traditionally the Vedas are Her command, which no one may transgress; dharma is what She has spoken.

meaning_check.note: The bahuvrīhi makes the Vedas the form of Her command ('Her own commands are the Vedas'); 'vedas' capitalized.

names.previous_split_issues: nijājñā was left fused; it is nijā + ājñā.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and itaretara-dvandva)
samasa.vigraha: पुण्यम् च अपुण्यम् च पुण्यापुण्ये; पुण्यापुण्ययोः फलम् पुण्यापुण्यफलम्; पुण्यापुण्यफलम् प्रददाति इति पुण्यापुण्यफलप्रदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: puṇyam ca apuṇyam ca puṇyāpuṇye; puṇyāpuṇyayoḥ phalam puṇyāpuṇyaphalam; puṇyāpuṇyaphalam pradadāti iti puṇyāpuṇyaphalapradā
samasa.explanation: (1) puṇya-apuṇya 'merit and demerit' (dvandva). (2) …puṇya-phala 'their fruit' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -pradā 'giving' is the head and governs the fruit as its object.

names.meaning: She who dispenses the fruits of both good and evil actions
names.significance: Actions do not reward themselves; traditionally it is She, as the Lord who governs karma, who brings each deed to its fruit.
names.previous_split_issues: puṇyāpuṇya was left fused; it is puṇya + apuṇya.

sandhi.rule: irregular fusion: in the sense 'hair-parting' sīman (its n dropped) + anta gives sīmanta, the second vowel replacing the first (pararūpa; the śakandhu group of words)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and gati-compound layers)
samasa.vigraha: श्रुतीनाम् सीमन्ताः श्रुतिसीमन्ताः; पादौ अब्जे इव पादाब्जे; पादाब्जयोः धूलिका पादाब्जधूलिका; असिन्दूरम् सिन्दूरम् कृता सिन्दूरीकृता; श्रुतिसीमन्तेषु सिन्दूरीकृता पादाब्जधूलिका यस्याः सा श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: śrutīnām sīmantāḥ śrutisīmantāḥ; pādau abje iva pādābje; pādābjayoḥ dhūlikā pādābjadhūlikā; asindūram sindūram kṛtā sindūrīkṛtā; śrutisīmanteṣu sindūrīkṛtā pādābjadhūlikā yasyāḥ sā śrutisīmantasindūrīkṛtapādābjadhūlikā
samasa.explanation: (1) śruti-sīmanta 'the hair-partings of the Vedas', the Vedas pictured as women (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) pāda-abja 'lotus feet' (feet like lotuses) and …abja-dhūlikā 'the dust of those feet' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) sindūrī-kṛta 'made into vermilion', a cvi formation: sindūra + kṛta with a → ī, meaning 'turned into what it was not' (Pāṇini 7.4.32). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She the dust of whose lotus feet is made the vermilion in the hair-partings of the Vedas'.

names.meaning: She the dust of whose lotus feet becomes the vermilion in the hair-parting of the Vedas
names.significance: The Vedas, pictured as married women, bow their heads at Her feet so that the dust of Her feet marks their partings like the vermilion of the auspicious wife: the Upaniṣads, the crown of the Veda, rest at Her feet.

meaning_check.note: Wording tidied (the doubled 'who is the one'); 'vermillion' misspelt; ITRANS 'shruti devatAs' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: sindūrī was glossed 'vermilion' without the cvi sense ('made into vermilion'); pādābja was left fused (pāda + abja).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23) and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class, n before d (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and rūpaka layers), applied to Her with the feminine -ā
samasa.vigraha: सकलाः आगमाः सकलागमाः; सकलागमानाम् सन्दोहः सकलागमसन्दोहः; शुक्तेः सम्पुटम् शुक्तिसम्पुटम्; सकलागमसन्दोहः एव शुक्तिसम्पुटम् सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटम्; तस्य मौक्तिकम् इव सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: sakalāḥ āgamāḥ sakalāgamāḥ; sakalāgamānām sandohaḥ sakalāgamasandohaḥ; śukteḥ sampuṭam śuktisampuṭam; sakalāgamasandohaḥ eva śuktisampuṭam sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭam; tasya mauktikam iva sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭamauktikā
samasa.explanation: (1) sakala-āgama 'all the scriptures' (karmadhāraya) and …āgama-sandoha 'their whole mass' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) śukti-sampuṭa 'the closed pair of oyster-valves' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The mass of scripture IS that oyster-shell (a karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (4) mauktika 'pearl' is the head, with the shell in the genitive: She is the pearl within; it takes the feminine -ā as applied to Her.

components.meaning: the closed hollow of two valves, a casket

names.meaning: She who is the pearl within the oyster-shell formed by all the scriptures together
names.significance: The scriptures enclose and guard Her as the shell guards the pearl: their whole worth lies in what they hold, and what they hold is She.

meaning_check.note: sandoha 'the whole collection' and sampuṭa 'the closed shell' rendered.

names.previous_split_issues: sakalāgama was left fused (sakala + āgama).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: पुरुषस्य अर्थाः पुरुषार्थाः; पुरुषार्थान् प्रददाति इति पुरुषार्थप्रदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: puruṣasya arthāḥ puruṣārthāḥ; puruṣārthān pradadāti iti puruṣārthapradā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: puruṣa-artha 'the aims of a person' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). Outer layer: -pradā 'giving' is the head and governs them as its object.

names.meaning: She who grants the (four-fold) objects of human life
names.significance: The four aims are dharma (right living), artha (wealth), kāma (fulfilled desire) and mokṣa (liberation); She grants each in its place, and the last above all.
names.previous_split_issues: puruṣārtha was left fused (puruṣa + artha).

names.meaning: She who is full and complete
names.significance: The Upaniṣadic invocation 'pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam' describes Her: whole, and whole even when the whole is taken from Her. Traditionally She neither grows nor decays, unlike the moon.

meaning_check.note: 'Without growth or decay' is a traditional gloss, moved to significance; the name says 'full, complete'.

names.meaning: She who is the enjoyer
names.significance: Traditionally all experience is finally Hers: She is the one who enjoys in every enjoyer.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: भुवनानाम् ईश्वरी भुवनेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhuvanānām īśvarī bhuvaneśvarī
samasa.explanation: īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head and bhuvana 'world' stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the worlds'.

names.meaning: She who is the ruler of the universe
names.significance: Bhuvaneśvarī is also the Goddess whose seed-syllable is hrīṃ (name 301), worshipped among the great Wisdom Goddesses.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is bhuvana + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

names.meaning: She who is the Mother, Ambikā
names.significance: Ambikā is the Mother of all the worlds; traditionally the name is also read as the union of Her three powers of will, knowledge and action.

meaning_check.note: 'Of the universe' is not in the name; it is moved to significance.

samasa.vigraha: आदिः च निधनम् च आदिनिधने; न विद्येते आदिनिधने यस्याः सा अनादिनिधना
samasa.vigraha_iast: ādiḥ ca nidhanam ca ādinidhane; na vidyete ādinidhane yasyāḥ sā anādinidhanā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: ādi 'beginning' and nidhana 'end' (dvandva). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi with the negative particle (nañ, appearing as an- before a vowel): 'She for whom beginning and end do not exist'. nidhana takes the feminine -ā.

components.note: appears as an- before a vowel
nidhana (ni + √dhā 'to put down'), with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who has neither beginning nor end
names.significance: What has a beginning has an end; She has neither, because time itself arises in Her.
names.previous_split_issues: nidhanā was glossed 'without end'; nidhana means 'end' — the 'without' is the an- that negates both ādi and nidhana.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: हरिः च ब्रह्मा च इन्द्रः च हरिब्रह्मेन्द्राः; हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रैः सेविता हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रसेविता
samasa.vigraha_iast: hariḥ ca brahmā ca indraḥ ca haribrahmendrāḥ; haribrahmendraiḥ sevitā haribrahmendrasevitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: hari-brahma-indra 'Hari, Brahmā and Indra' (dvandva; brahman drops its final n). Outer layer: the past participle sevitā 'served, attended' is the head and takes the gods in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who is attended by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra
names.significance: The highest gods are Her attendants; their powers are Her gifts.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'brahmA', 'viShNu' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: brahmendra was given as one row; it is brahma + indra, joined by guṇa.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside nārāyaṇa; the n of ayana then becomes ṇ after r (retroflexion)

components.note: feminine of nārāyaṇa = nāra 'the waters' (or 'beings') + ayana 'resting-place'

names.meaning: She who is the feminine counterpart of Nārāyaṇa
names.significance: The Devī Māhātmya hymns Her with the refrain 'nārāyaṇi namo 'stu te'; as Nārāyaṇī She is Viṣṇu's own power (compare name 280).

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'nArAyaNa' put into IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; nārāyaṇī is the feminine of nārāyaṇa (nāra + ayana).

samasa.vigraha: नादः रूपम् यस्याः सा नादरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: nādaḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā nādarūpā
samasa.explanation: 'She whose form is nāda'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

components.meaning: nāda, sound; in Tantra the subtle, unstruck sound from which speech unfolds

names.meaning: She who is in the form of sound
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā nāda is the subtle resonance that rises after the bindu in the utterance of a seed-syllable such as hrīṃ, and from which all speech and all things unfold.

samasa.vigraha: नाम च रूपम् च नामरूपे; नामरूपाभ्याम् विवर्जिता नामरूपविवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: nāma ca rūpam ca nāmarūpe; nāmarūpābhyām vivarjitā nāmarūpavivarjitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: nāma-rūpa 'name and form' (dvandva; nāman drops its final n). Outer layer: vivarjitā 'wholly free from' is the head and takes them in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She who has no name or form
names.significance: In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (6.3) Being enters the world to unfold name and form; She is that Being, Herself untouched by name and form — even as She bears a thousand names.

sandhi.rule: m becomes the nasal of the following stop's class, ṅ before k (via anusvāra, Pāṇini 8.3.23 and 8.4.58)

components.meaning: hrīṃ, the seed-syllable (bīja) of the Goddess

components.note: -kāra, the suffix that names a sound, with the feminine -ī

names.meaning: She who is the syllable hrīṃ
names.significance: Hrīṃ, the māyā-bīja or Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja, closes each of the three sections of Her fifteen-syllabled mantra; the name can also be read 'She who makes the syllable hrīṃ'.

meaning_check.note: ITRANS 'hrIM' put into IAST; 'is the form of syllable' tidied.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; it is hrīm + kārī.

components.meaning: modesty, shyness; also the syllable hrīṃ

names.meaning: She who is endowed with modesty
names.significance: Traditionally modesty here is the reserve of the noble; the name can also be read 'She who possesses the syllable hrīṃ', continuing name 301.

components.meaning: dwelling in the heart; dear to the heart, pleasing
components.note: from hṛdaya 'heart' (as hṛd-, Pāṇini 6.3.50) + the suffix -ya, feminine

names.meaning: She who abides in the heart and delights it
names.significance: She is found in the heart of the devotee, and is what the heart finds dearest.

meaning_check.note: hṛdya is first 'dear to the heart' (Pāṇini 4.4.95 hṛdayasya priyaḥ); 'abiding in the heart' is also traditional, so both are given.

names.uncertain: Two derivations are current: 'dear to the heart' (4.4.95) and 'being in the heart'; the meaning gives both.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the prefixed word upādeya

samasa.vigraha: हेयम् च उपादेयम् च हेयोपादेये; हेयोपादेयाभ्याम् वर्जिता हेयोपादेयवर्जिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: heyam ca upādeyam ca heyopādeye; heyopādeyābhyām varjitā heyopādeyavarjitā
samasa.explanation: Inner layer: heya 'what is to be given up' and upādeya 'what is to be taken up' (dvandva of two gerundives). Outer layer: varjitā 'free from' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental: for Her there is nothing to reject and nothing to accept.

names.meaning: She who has nothing to reject or accept
names.significance: Since all is Her own self, nothing can be shunned or sought; the seeker's discipline of rejecting and accepting ends in Her.
names.previous_split_issues: heyopādeya was left fused; it is heya + upādeya, joined by guṇa.

verse_notes.note: Names 249–250 pair the five Brahmās (Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva): lifeless as Her seat, alive as Her form. Names 251–253 then name Her as consciousness and bliss.
Names 256–263 follow the states of the self in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad: waking (Viśva), dream (Taijasa), deep sleep (Prājña), the Fourth (turya) and beyond all states.
Names 264–274 set out the five cosmic acts with their deities: creation (Brahmā), protection (Govinda), dissolution (Rudra), concealment (Īśvara) and grace (Sadāśiva).

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ī + ī → ī (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā; the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a absorbed at the start of the next name

verse_notes.note: Bhāskararāya's division reads tirodhānakarīśvarī as two names, tirodhānakarī (270) and īśvarī (271): the long ī belongs to both. Likewise sadāśivā'nugrahadā is sadāśivā (272) + anugrahadā (273), the avagraha showing the elided a.
Name 277 Bhagamālinī is also the second of the fifteen Nityā goddesses; names 277 and 279 both turn on bhaga, the six divine excellences.
Name 281 fills the whole first half; names 282–284 echo the Puruṣa-sūkta ('sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt').
Name 285: ābrahma-kīṭa is 'from Brahmā down to the worm', the indeclinable ā + brahma, not a word ābrahma.
Each half is a single name (289, 290): the Vedas bowing to Her feet, and the scriptures as the shell that holds Her as a pearl.

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā; the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a absorbed at the start of the next name

verse_notes.note: Divide ambikā (295) | anādinidhanā (296): the avagraha marks the initial a of anādi, which carries the negation.
Names 301–302 open with hrī: hrīṅkārī is the seed-syllable hrīṃ, and hrīmatī can be read with it as well as 'modest'.

report.summary: Checked all 56 names of ślokas 61–70 (names 249–304) against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (including prefix junctions such as ut + meṣa and sam + doha), layered samāsa analyses with vigraha-vākyas in pausa form, and the meanings against that analysis. Two meanings were replaced (271 īśvarī, 279 bhagavatī: the old wording was not in the name) and one list of the five cosmic acts was corrected (274). External sandhi joins names in ślokas 64 and 69 (including Bhāskararāya's division of tirodhānakarīśvarī into 270 + 271). No problem was found in the Sanskrit text; svapantī (258) is noted as non-Pāṇinian but attested.
